note: Free, unmanaged TVA dispersed camping at the TN-92 (Chestnut Hill Rd) bridge over a Douglas Lake arm near Dandridge: gravel spots with fire rings on both sides of the highway, some beside the gravel boat ramp on the north side. Douglas is drawn down sharply in winter, leaving the bay as mud flats. Campers report trash, highway noise and a few long-term occupants; one listing gives a 20-ft RV limit. --Claude
summary: Moonhill Bridge: TVA camping/day-use/Douglas pages (headless; none names the site), rec.gov search (none), Campendium + Dyrt + RV Life (aggregators), Esri (winter) + USGS summer imagery, 3DEP read. Lakefront kept on geometry (pin clearing 1 m above summer pool, ~20-50 m over open apron). No operator page names it - inclusion rests on aggregators. Dyrt summary says 'RVs are limited to 20 feet'.
flags: INCLUSION / WEB PRESENCE: no TVA page names Moonhill Bridge (TVA's camping page lists only the six concession campgrounds plus 'camp in the wild on undeveloped TVA public lands'). Existence and use rest on aggregators: Campendium ($0 reported 2026-05-26), The Dyrt (connectivity check-ins 2026-11-23), RV Life listing. Kept under the small-free-dispersed-sites rule; reviewer's call.

RIG LENGTH (aggregator, not agency): The Dyrt's site-written summary says 'RVs are limited to 20 feet'; Campendium lists 'Big rigs'. No TVA source either way. Not a drop candidate on an aggregator line, but under ~23 ft would be out if TVA said it.

LONG-TERM OCCUPANTS: Dyrt review 2024-06-07 'there are a few people who live here'; summary 'semi-permanent resident presence'; Campendium 2023 'Very dirty, lots of trash and right off the highway.' Caveat put in the note.

WATERFRONT lakefront KEPT: no site numbers (dispersed). The camping clearing at the pin 35.95458,-83.36926 is 305.8 m on 3DEP, 1 m above Douglas's 304.8 m (1,000 ft) summer pool, which runs ~20 m south on 3DEP and ~40-55 m on the summer USGS orthophoto across an open grass/sand apron (gentle slope, passes the kayak test). Winter Esri imagery shows the bay as dry mud - the drawdown, not the shore.
